## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
It sets out proper etiquette regarding the consumption of meals, specifically proscribing the breaking up of mouthfuls of food [SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the rule has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
The rule forms part of a shared disciplinary heritage across early Buddhist traditions [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral identifies comprehensive parallels in the Pali *Bhikkhu Pātimokkha* (Sk 45), the *Bhikkhu Parivāra*, and the corresponding nun's rules in the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* and *Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha* [SuttaCentral]. In other Vinaya traditions, full parallels are preserved in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan recensions of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Lokottaravāda, and Kāśyapīya lineages [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus reflects the formulaic structure typical of the *Sekhiya* chapter, recording extensive Pali-internal text sharing with neighbouring rules including Sekhiya 48 (§0.1–1.17 ↔ §0.1–1.15), Sekhiya 47 (§1.1–1.17 ↔ §1.1–1.15), Sekhiya 46 (§0.1–1.17 ↔ §0.1–1.15), and Sekhiya 44 (§0.1–1.17 ↔ §0.1–1.16) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments computed by DharmaNexus also detect matches with the Tibetan *Vinayasamuccaya* (*Pratimokṣasūtraṭīkāvinayasamuccaya*, D4106-3) and the Sanskrit *Pravāraṇāvastu* [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
